distractorNotes: Paragraph 17 opens by saying none of this diminishes the science, so the criticism is aimed at one claim, not the field.
Paragraph 17 calls the symbiosis ancient, nearly universal and structurally elegant, which is the part it treats as settled.
The closing sentence points toward more work on the question, not away from the subject.

steps: Read the first and last lines of paragraph 17. The author's verdict sits there.
First line: "None of this diminishes the science." So the open questions are not a flaw.
Last line: "The gap is where the interesting work sits." An opening, not a stop sign.

choices.text: a sign that the whole field has been oversold
choices.note: Paragraph 16 says the popular telling outran the data. Paragraph 17 then opens: none of this diminishes the science. The field itself is not oversold.

choices.text: evidence that the symbiosis itself has been misdescribed
choices.note: Paragraph 17 lists the symbiosis as what is not in doubt: ancient, nearly universal and structurally elegant. The open question is the sharing.

choices.text: a reason to set the subject aside for the time being
choices.note: The author calls the gap where the interesting work sits, a reason to keep going. Setting the subject aside runs that line backward.

choices.text: a problem that no instrument will ever be able to settle
choices.note: The author calls the questions open, not unanswerable. Nothing in paragraph 17 says no instrument could ever settle them.
